sentences.nl: Mijn naam is Bart de Pau.

sentences.en: I am an online Dutch teacher.

sentences.nl: Vandaag oefenen we zinnen met de grammatica, van #dutchgrammar les 33 over reflexieve werkwoorden.
sentences.en: Today we are practicing sentences with the grammar from #dutchgrammar lesson 33 on reflexive verbs.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today practice we sentences with the grammar, from #dutchgrammar lesson 33 about reflexive verbs.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Oefenen" is a verb meaning "to practice" and is used in the present tense here.  
• "Met de grammatica" uses the preposition "met" (with) to indicate what is being practiced.  
• "Van #dutchgrammar les 33" shows possession or association, meaning "from #dutchgrammar lesson 33."  
• Reflexive verbs ("reflexieve werkwoorden") are verbs that require a reflexive pronoun.

Extra examples:  
– Morgen bespreken we het hoofdstuk over spreekwoorden. (Tomorrow we discuss the chapter about proverbs.)  
– We oefenen elke dag met de nieuwe woordenschat. (We practice every day with the new vocabulary.)  
– Ze leert nu over de Nederlandse cultuur. (She is now learning about Dutch culture.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Vandaag herhalen we de regels die we gisteren hebben geleerd. (Today we review the rules we learned yesterday.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific culture note applicable here.

sentences.nl: Het is pauze.
sentences.en: It is break time.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• It is break.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het is" is the Dutch equivalent of "it is," used to describe a state or condition.  
• "Pauze" is a noun meaning "break" or "pause," often used to refer to a break period, like recess or a coffee break.  
• Dutch sentences often follow a Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) order, as seen here.

Extra phrases:  
• "Het is laat." (It is late.)  
• "Het is tijd om te gaan." (It is time to go.)  
• "Het is belangrijk." (It is important.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Het is lunchtijd." (It is lunchtime.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch schools and workplaces, "pauze" typically refers to a short break period during which people can relax, eat, or socialize.

sentences.nl: De studenten staan buiten.
sentences.en: The students are standing outside.

sentences.nl: Ze praten met elkaar over hun eerste les.
sentences.en: They are talking to each other about their first lesson.

sentences.nl: En over het perfectum.
sentences.en: And about the perfect tense.

sentences.nl: Alle studenten kennen het perfectum goed.
sentences.en: All the students know the perfect tense well.

sentences.nl: Behalve Gianluca.
sentences.en: Except Gianluca.

sentences.nl: Hij kan zich de regels van het perfectum niet goed herinneren.
sentences.en: He cannot remember the rules of the perfect tense well.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He can himself the rules of the perfect tense not well remember.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij kan zich... herinneren" uses a reflexive verb structure, where "zich" refers back to the subject "hij."  
• The verb "herinneren" (to remember) requires a reflexive pronoun in Dutch when recalling something.  
• "Het perfectum" refers to the perfect tense, a common grammatical term used in language learning.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Zij kan zich de weg naar het station niet meer herinneren." (She can't remember the way to the station anymore.)  
  - "Wij kunnen ons de afspraak van morgen niet herinneren." (We can't remember the appointment for tomorrow.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hij kan zich het recept voor de taart niet herinneren." (He can't remember the recipe for the cake.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• There is no specific cultural note related to this sentence.

sentences.nl: Ik schaam me een beetje.
sentences.en: I am a little ashamed.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I shame myself a bit.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Schaam" is the verb "schamen," which means "to be ashamed." It's reflexive, so it uses "me" (myself).  
• Reflexive verbs in Dutch often require a reflexive pronoun like "me," "je," or "zich."  
• "Een beetje" means "a bit" or "a little," used to moderate the expression.

Examples:  
• Ik was me elke ochtend. (I wash myself every morning.)  
• Hij vergist zich vaak. (He often makes mistakes.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze schaamt zich voor haar fout. (She is ashamed of her mistake.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, expressing feelings of shame might be more direct than in some other cultures, reflecting a straightforward communication style.

sentences.nl: Jij? — Jij schaamt je? — Je vergist je!
sentences.en: You? — You are ashamed? — You are mistaken!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You? — You are ashamed? — You are mistaken!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Jij" is the informal singular pronoun for "you."  
• "Schaamt je" uses the reflexive verb "zich schamen," which means "to be ashamed." Reflexive verbs in Dutch often require a reflexive pronoun, here "je."  
• "Vergist je" uses the reflexive verb "zich vergissen," meaning "to be mistaken." Again, this requires the reflexive pronoun "je."

Extra phrases:  
• "Ik schaam me voor mijn fout." (I am ashamed of my mistake.)  
• "Zij vergist zich vaak in de datum." (She often mistakes the date.)  
• "Wij schamen ons niet voor onze keuzes." (We are not ashamed of our choices.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Jij? — Jij verveelt je? — Dat kan toch niet?" (You? — You are bored? — That can't be!)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, direct confrontation or expressions of surprise, such as questioning someone's feelings of shame or mistake, are not uncommon. The Dutch are known for their directness and valuing honesty in communication.

sentences.nl: Jij kent geen schaamte!
sentences.en: You have no shame!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You know no shame!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Jij" is the informal singular form of "you."  
• "Kent" is the second-person singular present tense of "kennen," which means "to know."  
• "Geen" is used to negate nouns, translating to "no" or "not any."  
• "Schaamte" means "shame."

• Extra phrases/sentences:  
  - "Hij heeft geen geld." (He has no money.)  
  - "Wij kennen het antwoord niet." (We don't know the answer.)  
  - "Zij voelt geen pijn." (She feels no pain.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij toont geen emoties." (She shows no emotions.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• None

sentences.nl: Ja Gianluca… je moet wel serieus zijn.
sentences.en: Yes Gianluca… you have to be serious.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Yes Gianluca… you must indeed serious be.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Je moet wel serieus zijn" uses "moet" as a modal verb meaning "must" or "have to," indicating necessity or obligation.  
• "Wel" in this context adds emphasis, similar to "indeed" or "definitely," suggesting that the speaker is reinforcing the necessity of being serious.  
• The verb "zijn" (to be) appears at the end of the clause, which is typical in Dutch subordinate or dependent clauses.

Extra phrases:  
• Je moet wel op tijd komen. (You must indeed come on time.)  
• Ze moet wel meer studeren. (She must indeed study more.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ja Lisa… je moet wel eerlijk zijn. (Yes Lisa… you must indeed be honest.)

sentences.nl: Dat zijn wij ook!
sentences.en: So are we!

sentences.nl: Anders gaat het tempo in de groep omlaag.
sentences.en: Otherwise, the pace in the group will slow down.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Otherwise goes the pace in the group down.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• This sentence uses inversion, which is common in Dutch when starting with an adverbial phrase like "anders" (otherwise). The verb "gaat" (goes) comes directly after "anders."  
• "Omlaag" is a direction word meaning "down." The verb "gaan" (to go) is commonly used with direction words.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Morgen gaan we naar het strand." (Tomorrow we go to the beach.)  
  - "Zonder jas wordt het koud." (Without a coat, it gets cold.)  
  - "Daarna ga ik naar huis." (Afterwards, I go home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Anders wordt het probleem groter." (Otherwise, the problem becomes bigger.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• [No culture note needed.]

sentences.nl: En dan vervelen wij ons.
sentences.en: And then we get bored.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And then bore we ourselves.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En dan" means "and then," where "dan" often indicates a sequence in time.  
• "Vervelen" means "to bore," and when reflexive ("zich vervelen"), it means "to be bored."  
• "Ons" is the reflexive pronoun for "wij" (we), showing that the action is done to ourselves.

Examples:  
• "Ik verveel me." (I am bored.)  
• "Hij verveelt zich tijdens de les." (He is bored during the lesson.)  
• "Wij vervelen ons nooit in de zomer." (We are never bored in the summer.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Na het eten wassen wij ons." (After dinner, we wash ourselves.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, the concept of "zich vervelen" is common among children and teenagers, especially during long summer holidays when structured activities might not be available.

sentences.nl: We kunnen misschien beter in het weekend uitgaan, Gianluca…, en niet vandaag.
sentences.en: We might be better off going out on the weekend, Gianluca…, and not today.

sentences.nl: We moeten ons niet haasten.
sentences.en: We must not rush.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• We must ourselves not hurry.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Moeten" is a modal verb meaning "must" and is used to express necessity or obligation.  
• "Ons" is a reflexive pronoun used here to indicate that the action of hurrying affects the subject.  
• The word order follows the typical Dutch structure with the reflexive pronoun following the modal verb, and the negation "niet" placed before the infinitive verb "haasten."  
• Example 1: "Je moet jezelf niet onder druk zetten." (You must not put yourself under pressure.)  
• Example 2: "Wij moeten ons voorbereiden op de vergadering." (We must prepare ourselves for the meeting.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ze moeten zich geen zorgen maken." (They must not worry.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: Ze praten over hun ‘geheim’.

sentences.nl: Zij denken dat Marieke gaat trouwen met Martin.
sentences.en: They think that Marieke is going to marry Martin.

sentences.nl: Maar ze vergissen zich.
sentences.en: But they are mistaken.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But they mistake themselves.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Maar" is a conjunction meaning "but," used to contrast with a previous statement.  
• "Ze" is a subject pronoun meaning "they."  
• "Vergissen zich" is a reflexive verb construction. "Vergissen" means "to mistake" or "to be mistaken," and "zich" is the reflexive pronoun that corresponds to "ze." In Dutch, many verbs require a reflexive pronoun to indicate that the action is performed on the subject itself.  
• Examples:  
  - "Ik vergis me." (I am mistaken.)  
  - "Hij vergist zich." (He is mistaken.)  
  - "Wij vergissen ons." (We are mistaken.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Jullie vergissen je vaak." (You often make mistakes.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Dutch people often use reflexive verbs in everyday speech, and it’s important to use the correct reflexive pronoun to match the subject.

sentences.nl: Lars heeft bij de barbecue gezegd:, Martin is ‘verliefd’ op Marieke.
sentences.en: Lars said at the barbecue, "Martin is 'in love' with Marieke."

sentences.nl: Maar ‘verliefd’ is niet hetzelfde als ‘verloofd’.
sentences.en: But 'in love' is not the same as 'engaged'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But 'in love' is not the same as 'engaged'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses a contrastive conjunction "maar" (but) to introduce a comparison.  
• The structure "is niet hetzelfde als" means "is not the same as" and is used for making comparisons.  
• The words "verliefd" (in love) and "verloofd" (engaged) are both adjectives. In Dutch, adjectives can be used as predicate adjectives after the verb "is" (is).  

Examples:  
– "Het boek is niet hetzelfde als de film." (The book is not the same as the movie.)  
– "Mijn huis is niet zo groot als jouw huis." (My house is not as big as your house.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Een hond is niet hetzelfde als een kat." (A dog is not the same as a cat.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No relevant culture note.

sentences.nl: En misschien is Marieke wel helemaal niet verliefd op Martin.
sentences.en: And maybe Marieke is not in love with Martin at all.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And maybe is Marieke indeed entirely not in love with Martin.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En" means "and" and is used to connect clauses.  
• "Misschien" means "maybe" and introduces uncertainty.  
• "Is" is a form of "zijn" (to be), used here as a linking verb.  
• "Wel helemaal niet" is a phrase that means "indeed not at all," emphasizing the negation.  
• "Verliefd op" means "in love with," where "op" is a preposition used with "verliefd" to indicate the object of affection.

Examples:  
- "En misschien komt hij morgen." (And maybe he will come tomorrow.)  
- "Zij is wel helemaal niet boos." (She is indeed not at all angry.)  
- "Hij is verliefd op haar." (He is in love with her.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Misschien is ze wel helemaal klaar met haar werk. (Maybe she is indeed completely done with her work.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• None

sentences.nl: ‘Psst… wie kent ons geheim?’ vraagt Soliman aan Xing.
sentences.en: Psst... who knows our secret?' Soliman asks Xing.

sentences.nl: Alleen ik, jij en Lars.
sentences.en: Only me, you, and Lars.

sentences.nl: OK. We mogen ons niet verspreken!
sentences.en: OK. We must not misspeak!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• OK. We may ourselves not misspeak!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Mogen" is a modal verb meaning "may" or "are allowed to," and it affects the meaning of the main verb "verspreken," which means "to misspeak."  
• "Ons niet verspreken" is a reflexive verb construction, where "ons" is the reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject "we."  
• The sentence is imperative in tone, despite not being structured as a command, emphasizing the importance of not making a mistake in speech.

• Examples:  
  - "We mogen ons niet vergissen." (We must not make a mistake.)  
  - "Je mag jezelf niet vergeten." (You must not forget yourself.)  
  - "Zij mogen zich niet haasten." (They must not hurry.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "We mogen ons niet laten afleiden." (We must not let ourselves be distracted.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.en: The other students must not know anything.

sentences.nl: Ik ben benieuwd.
sentences.en: I am curious.

sentences.nl: Martin komt hier op bezoek.
sentences.en: Martin is coming to visit here.

sentences.nl: Dat heeft Lars gezegd.
sentences.en: Lars said that.

sentences.nl: Oh… hier op het vakantiepark, zijn een paar hele romantische plekjes.
sentences.en: Oh... here at the holiday park, there are a few very romantic spots.

sentences.nl: Vooral ‘s avonds bij het meertje.
sentences.en: Especially in the evenings by the little lake.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Especially in the evening by the little lake.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vooral" means "especially" and is used to emphasize a particular part of the sentence.  
• "'s Avonds" is a contraction of "des avonds," which means "in the evening." It's a common way to indicate time.  
• "Bij het meertje" means "by the little lake," where "bij" is a preposition meaning "by" or "at," "het" is the definite article "the," and "meertje" is the diminutive form of "meer" (lake), indicating a small or endearing lake.

• Extra Sentences:  
  - "Vooral 's ochtends is het druk." (Especially in the morning, it is busy.)  
  - "Bij de rivier is het rustig." (By the river, it is quiet.)  
  - "We gaan vooral in de zomer op vakantie." (We mainly go on vacation in the summer.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Vooral 's middags bij het park. (Especially in the afternoon by the park.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No applicable cultural note.

sentences.nl: Daar is een bruggetje.
sentences.en: There is a little bridge.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• There is a small bridge.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daar" means "there" and is used to indicate location.  
• "is" is the third person singular form of "zijn" (to be).  
• "een" is the indefinite article "a" or "an".  
• "bruggetje" is a diminutive form of "brug" (bridge), indicated by the suffix "-je", which often conveys smallness or endearment.

Extra phrases:  
• "Daar staat een huis." (There stands a house.)  
• "Daar ligt een boek." (There lies a book.)  
• "Daar hangt een schilderij." (There hangs a painting.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Daar is een katje." (There is a kitten.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
-

sentences.nl: En als de maan schijnt over het water…
sentences.en: And when the moon shines over the water…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And if the moon shines over the water...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En" means "and," used to connect clauses or sentences.  
• "Als" means "if," introducing a condition or a conditional clause.  
• "De maan" means "the moon." In Dutch, nouns are often preceded by a definite article ("de" or "het").  
• "Schijnt" is the third-person singular present tense of "schijnen," meaning "to shine."  
• "Over" is a preposition meaning "over" or "above."  
• "Het water" means "the water." Here, "het" is the definite article for neuter nouns.  

Extra phrases:  
• "Als de zon ondergaat, wordt het donker." (If the sun sets, it gets dark.)  
• "De sterren schijnen helder in de nacht." (The stars shine brightly in the night.)  
• "Hij loopt over de brug." (He walks over the bridge.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En als de regen valt, blijven we binnen." (And if the rain falls, we stay inside.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, the moon and water often appear together in poetry and songs, reflecting the country's historical and cultural connection to water.

sentences.nl: Oh, wat romantisch!
sentences.en: Oh, how romantic!

sentences.nl: Misschien moet Lars een tip geven aan Martin.
sentences.en: Maybe Lars should give Martin a tip.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Maybe must Lars a tip give to Martin.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Misschien" (maybe) is an adverb that often starts a sentence to indicate possibility.  
• "Moet" is the present tense of "moeten" (must/should), which is a modal verb. Modal verbs are followed by an infinitive verb at the end of the clause.  
• "Een tip geven" literally means "to give a tip," using the noun "tip" (tip/advice) and the verb "geven" (to give).  
• "Aan" is a preposition used here to indicate the indirect object (Martin).

Examples:  
– Misschien moet ik een boek kopen. (Maybe I should buy a book.)  
– Je moet je huiswerk aan de leraar geven. (You must give your homework to the teacher.)  
– Hij moet een cadeau aan zijn vriendin geven. (He must give a gift to his girlfriend.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Misschien moet Anna een brief schrijven aan haar ouders. (Maybe Anna should write a letter to her parents.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• None

sentences.nl: Dan kent Martin dit romantische plekje.
sentences.en: Then Martin knows this romantic spot.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Dan knows Martin this romantic spot.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence structure follows the Subject-Verb-Object order typical in Dutch: "Dan kent Martin dit romantische plekje."  
• "Kent" is the present tense form of the verb "kennen," meaning "to know."  
• "Romantische" is an adjective describing "plekje" (spot), and it agrees in number and gender.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Ik ken haar nog niet." (I don't know her yet.)  
  - "Hij kent dat restaurant goed." (He knows that restaurant well.)  
  - "Dit is een mooi plekje." (This is a nice spot.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa kent het kleine café op de hoek. (Lisa knows the small café on the corner.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Romantische plekje" often refers to a place with sentimental or picturesque value, which could be common in a country known for its charming landscapes and historic cities.

sentences.nl: Dan kan hij Marieke meenemen.
sentences.en: Then he can take Marieke along.

sentences.nl: Samen naar de maan kijken op een warme zomeravond.
sentences.en: Watching the moon together on a warm summer evening.

sentences.nl: Wat een goed idee!
sentences.en: What a good idea!

sentences.nl: Nou… wat een emoties allemaal, bij de Dutch Summer School.
sentences.en: Well... what a lot of emotions at the Dutch Summer School.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Well... what an emotions all, at the Dutch Summer School.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Nou" is an interjection often used to express surprise or emphasis, similar to "well" or "wow" in English.  
• "Wat een" is used to express amazement or intensity, equivalent to "what a" in English.  
• "Allemaal" can mean "all" or "all of them," adding emphasis to the situation described.  
• "Bij" is a preposition meaning "at" or "with," indicating location or involvement.

Examples:  
• Wat een weer vandaag! (What a weather today!)  
• Bij de bakker is het druk. (It's busy at the baker's.)  
• Wat een prachtige bloemen allemaal! (What beautiful flowers all!)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Nou, wat een drukte allemaal, bij het concert! (Wow, what a crowd at the concert!)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Dutch Summer School is a popular program where people from around the world come to learn Dutch intensively during the summer. It's often an immersive experience with a focus on both language and culture.

sentences.nl: Dat wordt nog erg spannend.
sentences.en: That will be very exciting.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• That becomes yet very exciting.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dat wordt" uses the verb "worden," which means "to become." It's often used to talk about changes or future states.  
• "Nog" means "yet" or "still," indicating that something will continue or develop.  
• "Erg" is an adverb meaning "very." It intensifies the adjective "spannend" (exciting).  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Het wordt morgen koud." (It will be cold tomorrow.)  
  - "Zij wordt binnenkort moeder." (She will become a mother soon.)  
  - "Dit boek is erg interessant." (This book is very interesting.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Het concert wordt vast heel leuk. (The concert will surely be very fun.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, the phrase "Dat wordt spannend" is often used in anticipation of an event, expressing both excitement and uncertainty about the outcome.

sentences.nl: Hoe hard gaat Gianluca studeren? — Wat vinden de andere studenten van hem? — En dan natuurlijk Martin en Marieke…
sentences.en: How hard is Gianluca going to study? — What do the other students think of him? — And then, of course, Martin and Marieke…

sentences.nl: Hoe eindigt dit misverstand? — Blijf kijken naar de ‘Heb je zin?’ videos.
sentences.en: How does this misunderstanding end? — Keep watching the 'Heb je zin?' videos.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• How ends this misunderstanding? — Keep watching the 'Did you enjoy?' videos.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoe eindigt dit misverstand?" uses the present tense to ask about the conclusion of an event, which is common in Dutch for future events as well.  
• "Blijf kijken naar" uses the verb "blijven" (to stay, remain) combined with an infinitive to form a continuous action, similar to "keep doing" in English.

  - "Blijf lezen voor meer informatie." (Keep reading for more information.)

sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And the word 'stay' from my previous sentence, is an imperative!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En" starts the sentence as a conjunction, linking it to previous context.  
• "Het woord 'blijf'" is a noun phrase with "het" (the) as the definite article and "woord" (word) as the noun, followed by the quoted word.  
• "Uit mijn vorige zin" includes "uit" (from) as a preposition, "mijn" (my) as a possessive pronoun, and "vorige zin" (previous sentence) as a noun phrase.  
• "Is een imperatief" uses "is" as the verb "to be" in present tense, "een" (an) as an indefinite article, and "imperatief" as a noun meaning imperative.

Extra phrases:  
• "Het boek uit de bibliotheek is interessant." (The book from the library is interesting.)  
• "De vraag uit het examen was moeilijk." (The question from the exam was difficult.)  
• "Zij is een lerares." (She is a teacher.)
